name: open_high_low_v13
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: When NIFTY opens at 09:15:00 and the index cannot trade ABOVE its opening price for the first 30 seconds (6 consecutive 5-second bars where the high never exceeds the 09:15:00 open), it reveals heavy institutional selling conviction — every attempt to bid the index up from the open is immediately absorbed by sellers. This 'open equals high' persistence pattern on NIFTY indicates that one or more large participants (typically FIIs executing pre-market sell orders routed through DMA algorithms) are committed to selling from the opening tick, and the aggregated demand of all other market participants cannot push the index even 1 point above the open. The reverse holds for 'open equals low' — if NIFTY cannot trade below its opening price for 30 seconds, institutional buying is overwhelming all selling pressure. This directional conviction signal is fundamentally different from gap strategies (which trade the gap fill) and opening drive reversal (which fades the opening move). Here we trade WITH the opening institutional flow, riding the directional momentum that follows when the first 30 seconds reveal a one-sided market. On NIFTY specifically, the open=high/low pattern is more reliable than on individual stocks because the index aggregates flow across 50 constituents — for NIFTY itself to show open=high, the selling must be broad-based or the dominant constituent flow must be overwhelmingly directional. At 5-second resolution, we confirm the pattern after 30 seconds (6 bars) and enter immediately, capturing the acceleration phase as retail and algorithmic traders see the directional candle on their 1-minute and 5-minute charts and pile in over the next 60-120 seconds.

indicators.name: session_open
indicators.formula: open price of the first 5s bar at 09:15:00
indicators.purpose: The reference price for the open=high/low pattern. On NIFTY, the 09:15:00 opening price is set by the pre-open auction (09:00-09:08 order collection, 09:08-09:15 matching). This single price represents the equilibrium of all pre-market orders and is the benchmark against which we measure directional conviction.

indicators.name: open_high_persists
indicators.formula: ALL(high[i] <= session_open for i in last 6 bars)
indicators.purpose: Boolean flag: true when NIFTY has not traded above the opening price for 6 consecutive 5s bars (30 seconds). On a single 5s bar, open=high is meaningless noise — a single tick can create it. But if the HIGH of every bar for 30 seconds never exceeds the opening price, it means sustained selling pressure is capping the index. The 30-second window (6 bars) was chosen because: (a) it filters out the first 5-10 seconds of opening auction settlement noise where prices can spike briefly above/below open, (b) it's long enough for at least 2-3 buying attempts to have been made and failed, confirming genuine selling dominance, and (c) it's short enough to enter before the 1-minute candle closes — giving us a 30-second head start on 1-minute chart traders who would see the same bearish candle pattern.

indicators.name: open_low_persists
indicators.formula: ALL(low[i] >= session_open for i in last 6 bars)
indicators.purpose: Boolean flag: true when NIFTY has not traded below the opening price for 6 consecutive 5s bars. Mirror of open_high_persists for bullish conviction detection. If the LOW of every bar stays at or above the open for 30 seconds, institutional buying is providing a floor that sellers cannot breach.

indicators.name: opening_range_size
indicators.purpose: The magnitude of price movement in the first 30 seconds. This serves as a quality filter: if the opening range is less than 8 spot points, the open=high/low pattern may be due to a quiet, indecisive open rather than genuine directional conviction. On NIFTY, a 30-second range of 8+ spot points indicates active participation and meaningful price discovery, not just a stale opening print. Conversely, if the range exceeds 40 spot points, the open was gap-driven and the pattern is reflecting gap mechanics rather than sustained directional flow — different thesis entirely.

indicators.name: momentum_6
indicators.purpose: Distance from the opening price after 30 seconds. Confirms that the directional move has substance — the index should have moved at least 5 spot points away from the open in the conviction direction. Without this minimum distance, the open=high/low pattern could be 'true' but trivially so (price barely moved from open), which doesn't indicate the strong institutional flow we're trying to capture.

conditions: open_low_persists == true (NIFTY has NOT traded below its opening price for 30 seconds — institutional buying is providing a floor)
opening_range_size >= 8 spot points (the open is active, not stale — genuine price discovery is happening)
opening_range_size <= 40 spot points (not a gap-driven extreme that has different reversion dynamics)
momentum_6 >= 5 (NIFTY has moved at least 5 spot points above the open — the buying has directional substance, not just a flat hold at the open)
buy_ce.confirmation: The 7th bar (second 31-35) must also maintain low >= session_open — one additional bar confirming the pattern holds. This prevents entering on a pattern that breaks down on the very next bar after our 30-second observation window.

conditions: open_high_persists == true (NIFTY has NOT traded above its opening price for 30 seconds — institutional selling is capping the index)
momentum_6 <= -5 (NIFTY has moved at least 5 spot points below the open)
buy_pe.confirmation: The 7th bar must also maintain high <= session_open

exit.stop_rationale: The stop is placed at the invalidation of the thesis: if NIFTY reverses back through the opening price, the directional conviction signal was false. On NIFTY, the distance from entry to the opening price is typically 5-12 spot points (2.5-6 option points) after the 30-second confirmation window. A 5-point option stop accommodates a brief pullback toward the open (common in the 35-50 second window as early momentum traders take quick profits) while ensuring we exit if NIFTY actually crosses back through the opening price, which invalidates the entire one-sided flow thesis. The original strategy used the open price as the stop — we approximate this with 5 option points which corresponds to roughly 10 spot points, providing slightly more room than an exact open-price stop to avoid getting shaken out by the common 'test of the open' pattern that occurs 40-60 seconds into the session.
exit.target_rationale: When open=high/low holds for 30 seconds on NIFTY, the subsequent directional move over the next 1-3 minutes typically covers 20-45 spot points (10-22 ATM option points) as the institutional flow continues and momentum traders pile in after seeing the 1-minute candle complete. Target of 10 option points captures the middle of this range, achievable within 60-120 seconds in most cases. This gives 1:2 risk-reward. The original targeted 1.5x ATR(14) which on daily NIFTY is roughly 150+ spot points — appropriate for a 15-60 minute hold but far too ambitious for our 30-180 second window. Our 10-point target corresponds to the initial acceleration phase before the opening drive naturally decelerates around the 2-3 minute mark.
exit.eod_rule: flatten at 09:20 — this is strictly an opening-pattern strategy; the directional conviction signal loses meaning after the first 5 minutes as other market dynamics take over

filters.vix_filter: VIX between 13-28. Below 13, opening moves on NIFTY are too subdued (5-10 spot point first-minute range) for the open=high/low pattern to produce tradeable momentum — the 4-point breakeven is hard to overcome. Above 28, opening gaps and volatility are extreme enough that the open=high/low pattern is usually a gap artifact rather than sustained directional conviction.
filters.time_filter: ONLY 09:15:00-09:20:00 IST. This is exclusively an opening pattern — the institutional conviction at the very first tick is the edge. After 5 minutes, the opening flow has been absorbed and the signal is stale. Entry window is specifically bars 7-12 (seconds 31-60 after open) — we need 30 seconds to confirm the pattern and enter within the next 30 seconds.
filters.volume_filter: opening_range_size >= 8 spot points serves as the activity proxy. On NIFTY index, volume in the first 30 seconds is always high (opening auction settlement) and doesn't differentiate between conviction and noise — price range is a more reliable signal of directional commitment.
filters.trend_filter: None — this IS the trend signal for the opening session. The open=high/low pattern itself establishes the directional thesis.
filters.spread_filter: Skip if ATM option bid-ask > 3 points. At 09:15, option spreads are typically wider than mid-session (market makers haven't finished calibrating). A 3-point spread tolerance is necessary to avoid filtering out most valid signals, but wider spreads erode the edge significantly.

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium-low — open=high/low is a well-known retail pattern, but the 5s persistence confirmation (30 seconds of sustained pattern) with range-size quality filters differentiates from the naive single-bar version; the signal is structural (institutional flow) rather than technical (pattern recognition)

adaptation_notes: Five key adaptations from the original open_high_low_v1: (1) The most critical change: open=high/low is evaluated over 6 consecutive 5-second bars (30 seconds) rather than a single 1-minute bar. A single 5s bar with open=high is pure noise — it happens randomly on ~50% of bars. The 30-second persistence requirement transforms this from a single-bar pattern into a sustained directional conviction signal. This is NOT a lookback scaling; it's a fundamental redesign of how the pattern is defined at higher temporal resolution. (2) Added opening_range_size filter (8-40 spot points) that the original lacked. This filters out false signals from quiet opens (where open=high holds trivially because nothing is trading) and gap-driven extremes (where the pattern reflects gap mechanics, not sustained flow). On NIFTY specifically, the 8-point minimum ensures the first 30 seconds had genuine institutional participation. (3) Added momentum_6 minimum (5 spot points from open) to confirm directional substance. The original had no distance filter — at 1-min resolution, open=high on a bar implicitly means some range occurred. At 5s, we need to explicitly verify the pattern has price movement behind it. (4) Session window compressed from first-15-minutes to first-5-minutes (09:15-09:20). The original allowed entries through 09:35 — on 1-min bars, the open=high/low pattern takes 1-15 minutes to materialize. At 5s resolution, we detect and confirm the pattern in 30 seconds, so the relevant window is much shorter. After 5 minutes, the opening flow has been fully absorbed and the conviction signal is stale. (5) Hold time compressed from 15-60 bars on 1-min (15-60 minutes) to 30-180 seconds. We target the initial acceleration phase of the opening directional move, exiting before the first pullback/consolidation that typically occurs 2-3 minutes after the open. The original's longer hold captured multiple waves of the opening trend; we capture only the first and most reliable wave.
weaknesses: Extremely low trade frequency — at most 1 trade per day, and the pattern only triggers on perhaps 30-40% of sessions, yielding roughly 5-8 trades per month. This means very high variance and slow statistical convergence for backtesting

Opening 5-second bars on NIFTY can have stale or erratic prints as the pre-open auction settles — the first 2-3 bars may show artificial open=high/low patterns from auction mechanics rather than genuine directional flow

Option spreads at 09:15 are the widest of the session (3-5 points on ATM NIFTY options vs. 1-2 points mid-session), consuming a significant portion of the expected 10-point target and potentially turning winners into losers

On gap-up open=low days (NIFTY gaps up AND holds above the open), the signal is bullish but the gap fill risk creates a ceiling — the strategy can get caught between bullish flow and gap-fill selling pressure

The 30-second confirmation window means we enter at least 30 seconds into the opening move, potentially missing the first 5-10 spot points of the directional acceleration and entering near the point where early momentum traders begin taking profits
